title: Amagi Media Labs Ltd - 544679 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Amagi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, a record, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 11.5% versus 5% a year ago.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR 437 crore, up 32% reported and 21% in constant currency, and almost 10% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose from INR 17 crore to INR 50 crore, with margin expanding to 11.5% despite the seasonally weak Q1 from annual increments. PAT rose to INR 34 crore (7.5% margin), and would have been about INR 40 crore excluding a one-time non-cash FX charge. Management reiterated operating leverage, highlighted AI product wins, and said gross margin will be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year.

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 249 crore, +39% YoY, driven by existing customer expansion, ~10,000 channel deliveries and 451 distributors (+21%).

segments.name: Monetization and Marketplace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, +30% YoY, volume-driven; monetized ad impressions a record 13.6 billion, +59% YoY and +21% QoQ.

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% reported; management said ~32% excluding the prior-year rev rec benefit from a large deal.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin to be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year, with Q3 seasonally strong; management described it as not structural deterioration.

Management is focused on full-year profitability rather than quarterly margins; H1 was ~47% of FY26 revenue and ~37% of FY26 adjusted EBITDA, indicating back-half EBITDA weighting (historical context, not guidance).
Q2 YoY comparison carries ~600 bps headwind from prior-year rev rec timing benefit; management said Q2 may not be the best marker for growth.
Broader AI product suite to be announced at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27; AI revenue contribution expected more visibly in late FY27.
Aspiration to maintain growth rates through the year, without explicit guidance.
capex_capacity: Cloud cost optimisation delivered ~USD 282,000 monthly run-rate gross margin savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives.
Live event delivery supported 104 FIFA World Cup matches on Amagi infrastructure for key customers; one US broadcaster received 100% on-air availability across 325 events and 450 hours.
Q1 is the weakest cash quarter each year due to incentive payouts, increments and software renewals.
Since January, 33 M&A opportunities evaluated, 23 passed on, 10 under active evaluation; management said this is not a signal of an imminent deal.
demand_pricing: Content processed reached 959,000 hours, +43% YoY; deliveries reached 9,900+ endpoints; distributors ~451, +21%.
Ad impressions 13.6 billion in the quarter, +59% YoY; management said FIFA did not add ad insertion upside and growth is organic (CTV penetration).

AI: 10+ active pilots; a major US news network selected Newspulse (agentic newsroom platform) after an earlier first paying customer; AI credit model introduced for some media operations, with outcome-based pricing possible later.
Pricing: one customer received a price adjustment but volume run-rate is >30% growth, a net revenue tailwind; management sees no material AI-driven deflation to revenue or pipeline yet.
Customer base: 400+ content providers, 400+ distributors, 80+ advertisers; logo churn in low single digits; top 10 customer average vintage ~5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the sequential gross margin improvement and will it recover to 69%? What is AI's impact on gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gross margin to 67% to 69% for this year, citing mix, live events, pricing and AI costs. AI is a small base with no substantial margin impact yet; a 2 to 3 year S-curve with a possible initial dip is expected. Gross margin was ~64% three to four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Do distribution platform additions drive customer growth, and is in-sourcing a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Several distribution platforms (Vodafone, Kogan TV, Virgin UK) became customers, but it is not a prerequisite. Management sees platforms outsourcing rather than in-sourcing and is not aware of in-sourcing impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross retention (GRR) disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: GRR is not disclosed; management pointed to logo churn in low single digits and top 10 customer vintage of ~5 years as stickiness indicators.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being priced and how is cost inflation protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage; AI credits model mirrors a cost-plus approach for agentic media operations, with telemetry built with Newspulse customer to measure cost and revenue benefit. Business model not yet settled; a few more quarters needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is NRR constant currency and what is the growth impact of last year's one-time item?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR is in reported currency on a TTM basis, as in the DRHP; full-year NRR to be disclosed at Q4. The prior-year rev rec benefit affected growth by ~450 bps. Management aspires to sustain growth but Q2 will still lap the base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Can channel deliveries be split between new channels and additional deliveries on existing channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Not tracked internally; directionally growth is from existing channels going to more deliveries. Net revenue retention contributed ~26 points of the ~31% growth from existing customers.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from live event mix, customer pricing and AI costs; guided to 67% to 69%.
Cash burn remains negative in Q1 (operating outflow INR 65 crore reported), with DSO improvement of ~8 days QoQ still needed.
Q2 FY27 faces a ~600 bps headwind from the prior-year rev rec base; growth optics may be weaker.
Monetisation of AI products (Newspulse and broader Q2 suite) is still early; revenue contribution expected late FY27.
Capital deployment: active M&A pipeline (10 opportunities under evaluation) against INR 1,616 crore cash.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 17 crore (5% margin) YoY; margin +1.2 pp QoQ
from INR 4 crore (1.1% margin) YoY; ~INR 40 crore excluding one-time non-cash FX charge
from INR 141 crore YoY; excluding one-time items INR 41 crore vs INR 84 crore

key_quotes: Gross margin will move with mix. We will keep optimizing cloud costs.
This is not a structural deterioration.
So, it has no correlation whatsoever with the FIFA World Cup, for example, from an organic growth standpoint.
But it's very early, like what Vijay is pointing out today, but that's the direction we're seeing.
So next quarter might not be the best marker because we'll still be lapping that base effect.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating leverage, margin expansion and customer trust, with AI described as early and monetisation timing left open. Management was cautious and deflective on gross margin structure, GRR disclosure, channel-delivery split and AI pricing, saying those metrics are not tracked or the model is not yet settled.

growth.why: No revenue growth number guided; management only gave an aspiration to maintain growth rates, gross margin guided at 67-69% for FY27, and growth is backed by demand (ad impressions +59%, content hours +43%) and pricing/volume rather than specific capacity or orders.
